elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, in whole or in part, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to HDI." The Company is our party; no Order Forms exist in this agreement structure, so the Agreement-level right is the full scope available.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right requires "ninety (90) days' prior written notice", three times the preferred 30-day maximum. To meet the preferred level the notice period in the new sentence would have to read thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered text; Section 4.2 only runs money the other way (Company pays HDI a Termination Payment). A pro-rata refund obligation on HDI for prepaid fees would have to be added.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1's mutual 90-day notice operates to stop the automatic one-year renewal on each anniversary; under the rule boundary, natural-term non-renewal is assessed under RENEWAL and is not a mid-term convenience right. No other clause gives HDI a mid-term no-cause exit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: New operative sentence grants the Company an unconditional convenience right "at any time" on "ninety (90) days' prior written notice", which sits at the top of the 60–90 day band.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) as amended: "provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed three (3) months of the fees payable by the Company under Section 3.1." The proviso overrides the retained twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000 / 2 formula and is anchored to an existing, resolvable fee provision.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: HDI's only no-cause exit is the Section 4.1 anniversary right: the Agreement "shall be automatically renewed ... unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" — i.e. a right to block renewal at the end of each one-year term, not a mid-term walk-away. Note the residual ambiguity in "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated"; if HDI later argues that notice can name any mid-term date, this element would fail, so consider adding "effective only at the end of the then-current term" to HDI's side.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 requires "ninety (90) days written notice" from either Party, so HDI's non-renewal/termination notice meets the 90-day floor.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the inserted Company convenience right (90 days) plus the three-month cap on the Termination Payment fill the two gaps, and HDI's existing Section 4.1 right already satisfies both Vendor-side elements as an end-of-term, 90-day non-renewal right.

Preferred is not reached: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; the rationale correctly declines to press it, so 'deviation' with a fallback-level redline is the right classification.

Minimality holds: two surgical edits (one concise inserted sentence, one proviso) into a clause that previously granted the Company no in-term exit; the existing formula, the '(if any)' language and the quarterly instalment mechanic in 4.2(b)-(c) are all retained, and no unrelated words were deleted or paraphrased.

Borderline surplus to note: "in whole or in part" is carried over from model language but there are no Order Forms here, and partial termination sits awkwardly with a Termination Payment computed on aggregate Net Sales. Deleting those four words would tighten minimality without weakening the position.

Intent preserved: the cap is tied to an existing, resolvable cross-reference (Section 3.1 fee obligation), the Termination Date definition in 4.1 still functions for the new right, and no retained sentence contradicts the insertion.
Negotiation note (not a defect): 90 days is the least Customer-favourable end of the 60–90 band; opening at 60 days costs nothing and remains within the fallback.
